citation: Sanjalawe Y, Al-E'mari S, Alqurashi T, Alharbi ZH, Makhadmeh SN, Alsharaiah M. Adaptive graph attention-based federated learning for IoT intrusion detection: mitigating poisoning attacks. PeerJ Computer Science 11:e3281, 2025. doi:10.7717/peerj-cs.3281

A1.evidence: No split method or proportions in 'Proposed methodology' / 'Experiments and results'; only 'identical configurations for dataset splits' (Measurement setup).

A2.evidence: Data matrix 'Rows represent packet sequences or time intervals (e.g., 1-s window)'; Table 6 CNN-GRU input 'Input sequence of network flows', GRU 'Captures temporal dependencies'; split not described.

A3.evidence: Stage 1: 'mean (μ) and standard deviation (σ) required for Z-score normalization are computed independently using each client's private dataset'; whether test data are excluded is not stated.

A4.evidence: Rounds, local epochs, batch size and learning rate not given anywhere (Tables 3-7 give hardware and layer specs only).

A5.evidence: Measurement setup: 'all experiments were executed on the same hardware infrastructure ... using identical configurations for dataset splits, local training epochs, model sizes, and communication rounds.'

A6.evidence: Table 12: FedAvg, FedGen, AdaptFL with bootstrap 95% CIs and 'p-values derived from paired t-tests against the AGAT-FL results'; Table 15 runtime per round for FedAvg etc. No statement that numbers were copied.

A7.evidence: Metrics defined: Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1-score (Tables 8-11); no MCC/balanced accuracy/G-mean.

A8.evidence: No client partition scheme given; only 'Local normalization also reflects the inherent non-IID nature of federated data distributions' (Stage 1).

A9.evidence: 'Statistical analysis and interpretation': 95% CIs 'estimated using bootstrap sampling (1,000 iterations), and p-values derived from paired t-tests' (Tables 12-13); ablation 'over five independent runs'.

A10.evidence: N-BaIoT and CIC-ToN-IoT evaluated separately (Tables 8-11); no cross-dataset test.

A11.evidence: Only Kaggle dataset links given; no code link in the visible text.

notes: Read the PeerJ HTML via the web-fetch tool. The fetched text was truncated in 'Discussion and limitations' (mid-sentence), so the Conclusion, Data Availability and Supplemental Information sections (where PeerJ normally lists code) were NOT visible; A11 'no' must be checked by the second coder. ResearchGate returned 429 and academia.edu gave the same truncated text. Borderline items: A5 'same' rests on the measurement-setup sentence (located in the overhead-analysis subsection but worded as 'all experiments'), and no round/epoch values are given. A6 'rerun' is not stated in words; it rests on the paired t-tests and CIs for baselines (Table 12) and the per-round baseline runtimes (Table 15). Table 8 cites baselines to papers that (per the tables) are mismatched (e.g. 'ScaleFL (McMahan et al., 2017)', 'FedAvg (Ilhan, Su & Liu, 2023)'). A9: number of runs behind the main-comparison t-tests is not stated. Table 4 CNN spec says 'Input: 32x32x3 (e.g., CIFAR-10)'.
